fields.why: No Yemeni quantities are given; the Saudi-Yemen contrast is a qualitative remark the article itself says cannot be made directly, so there is no comparison of outcome quantities.

An outbreak update; case finding through the referral system is part of the investigation, but reading the case counts as surveillance/descriptive is also defensible.
Case counts come from the Saudi MOH's reporting system, which the brief classes as international surveillance; 'other' fits the entomologic and ungulate serosurveys, not the case system.

Citizenship (Saudi/Yemeni/other) among cases is a nativity descriptor, giving level 1; A treated it as part of the international setting. A rule stating that nationality of cases within an international report still counts as nativity would decide it.
Same issue: citizenship counts are reported verbatim and fit the nativity dimension as descriptor.

brief_issues: Brief says an international setting is not an equity reading but does not say whether case nationality/citizenship within an international report counts as nativity. B correctly flagged province shares (365 [77%] of 516) that do not reconcile.
